predecessors.name: Roman Empire
predecessors.text: Palmyra and the Roman East that Odaenathus held after the defeat at Edessa: 'ruled Syria' under a nominal Roman framework, 'from the Pontic coast in the north to Palestine in the south' (Odaenathus…

successors.name: Roman Empire
successors.text: Palmyra, garrisoned in 272 and razed in 273 after the revolt of Septimius Apsaios; the rest of the empire returned to Aurelian in 272

ledger.x: 262: Odaenathus carries the war to the Persians.
267: the Persian war ends with Odaenathus.
270: the Palmyrene kingdom becomes an empire.
273: Palmyra rebels under Septimius Apsaios, proclaims Antiochus Augustus, and Aurelian 'spared Antiochus, but razed Palmyra'; the infobox 'Disestablished: 273'.

wars.name: Odaenathus against Macrianus and Quietus
wars.outcome: Odaenathus sided with Gallienus; the Emesans killed Quietus as he approached in early 261 and Balista was captured and executed in autumn 261; Syria stayed under Odaenathus.

wars.name: Odaenathus's Persian wars
wars.outcome: After driving Shapur I out of Syria in late summer 260 he retook Edessa, Carrhae and Nisibis in spring 262, besieged Ctesiphon in late 262 or early 263 and again in 266 and broke off to face Germanic raiders; Gallienus took the title Persicus maximus after…

wars.name: Palmyrene conquests of Arabia, Egypt and Galatia
wars.outcome: Zenobia's generals took Roman Arabia (Bosra), Egypt (Probus defeated at Babylon Fortress) and Galatia; Chalcedon held out.

wars.name: Aurelian's reconquest of the Palmyrene Empire
wars.outcome: Aurelian crossed the Bosphorus, beat Zenobia at Immae and Emesa, took Antioch, besieged Palmyra in the summer of 272 and razed it in 273 after the revolt under Septimius Apsaios.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines; the extents are provinces named without boundaries, and the Anatolian edge is undated beyond Galatia.
